description: Blockchains built up from their parts: hashes and Merkle trees, blocks and chains, consensus by proof of work and proof of stake, keys, wallets and transactions, smart contracts, and a clear-eyed look at real use cases, limits and regulation, with a small blockchain implemented and a contract deployed to a test network. Taught to the depth of a leading blockchain technologies course.
modelledOn: Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten, Miller and Goldfeder, Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies
Nakamoto, Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System
outcomes: Explain and implement the cryptographic building blocks of a blockchain: hashes, Merkle trees, digital signatures.
Describe how blocks, chains, forks and confirmations give tamper-evidence and how a longest-chain rule resolves conflicts.
Compare proof of work, proof of stake and permissioned consensus and analyse their security and energy assumptions.
Create keys and wallets, construct and verify transactions, and explain the UTXO and account models.
Write, test and deploy a smart contract and identify common vulnerabilities.
Evaluate blockchain proposals for land registry, supply chain and payments against simpler alternatives, and summarise the regulatory position.

units.title: Hashing and Merkle trees
topics: Cryptographic hash properties; SHA-256 and Keccak; hash pointers and tamper-evident lists
Merkle trees: construction, proofs of inclusion, light clients
Digital signatures with ECDSA and secp256k1; public keys as identities
Commitments and puzzles; implementing hashes, Merkle proofs and signatures in code

units.title: Blocks, chains and immutability
topics: Block structure: header, previous hash, Merkle root, nonce, timestamp, difficulty
Chaining, forks, orphan blocks, confirmations; why rewriting history is expensive
Peer-to-peer networking: gossip, block and transaction propagation, nodes and miners
Building a minimal blockchain in Python or JavaScript and attacking it
Distributed ledgers versus databases: what immutability does and does not give you

units.title: Proof of work and proof of stake
topics: The double-spend problem and Byzantine agreement among strangers; the Nakamoto consensus
Proof of work: mining, difficulty adjustment, hash rate, pools, 51 percent attacks, selfish mining, energy consumption
Proof of stake: validators, staking, slashing, finality (Casper, Tendermint); nothing-at-stake and long-range attacks
Permissioned consensus: PBFT, Raft-based ledgers (Hyperledger Fabric)
Comparing security, decentralisation, throughput and energy; the scalability trilemma

units.title: Wallets, keys and transactions
topics: Key generation, addresses, hierarchical deterministic wallets, seed phrases, custody and loss
Transactions: inputs and outputs (UTXO model), scripts, fees, mempool; the account model in Ethereum
Constructing, signing and verifying a transaction by hand; multisignature and time locks
Exchanges, stablecoins, and how cedis move into and out of crypto; the risks of custodial services

units.title: Smart contracts
topics: Ethereum: the EVM, gas, accounts, state; Solidity basics: types, functions, events, modifiers
Writing, testing (Hardhat or Foundry) and deploying a contract to a test network; interacting from a web page
Token standards (ERC-20, ERC-721) and decentralised applications; oracles
Vulnerabilities: reentrancy (The DAO), integer issues, access control, front-running; auditing and formal verification in brief
Layer-2 scaling: payment channels, rollups; cross-chain bridges

units.title: Use cases: land registry, supply chain, payments
topics: Land registry: Ghana's land title problems, the Bitland pilot, what a ledger can and cannot fix (garbage in, legal recognition)
Supply chain provenance: cocoa and pharmaceuticals; the oracle problem; IBM Food Trust lessons
Payments and remittances: cross-border transfers, stablecoins, central bank digital currencies (e-Cedi), mobile money comparison
Identity, voting, academic credentials and other proposals; a decision framework: do you need a blockchain?
Enterprise ledgers: Hyperledger Fabric and permissioned deployments

units.title: Limitations and regulation
topics: Limits: throughput, latency, energy, privacy on public ledgers, key loss, upgradeability, governance
Scams, fraud and consumer harm; AML/KYC and the travel rule
Regulation: Bank of Ghana and SEC positions, the e-Cedi, international approaches (MiCA, FATF)
Capstone: a complete decentralised application with a report on whether a blockchain was the right choice

schedule.title: Hashes and Merkle trees
schedule.exercise: Hash five short messages with the hashing tool, record the digests, then write a half-page explanation of why each of preimage, second-preimage and collision resistance matters for a ledger.

tasks.title: Compute SHA-256 digests of ten short strings, change one character in each, and record how many output bits flip to demonstrate the avalanche effect
Build a Merkle tree over eight transactions step by step, then produce and verify an inclusion proof for transaction five using only sibling hashes
Build a hash-pointer list of 20 records, then find and repair a tampered record using only the stored head hash and a verification routine

schedule.title: Signatures, commitments and puzzles
schedule.exercise: Written exercise: explain why a public key can serve as an identity, and describe what an attacker gains from reusing an ECDSA nonce.

tasks.title: Generate an ECDSA secp256k1 key pair, sign a short message, verify the signature, and show that verification fails after changing one byte
Implement a hash commitment scheme with a random salt, then show that the commitment hides the value yet binds the committer to it
Implement a proof-of-work puzzle with adjustable leading-zero difficulty and measure average attempts over 50 runs for difficulties 1 to 5

schedule.title: Blocks, chains and the network
schedule.exercise: Draw a block header diagram with field sizes and write a short account of how a transaction travels from a phone wallet to a confirmed block.

tasks.title: Create a block data structure with previous hash, Merkle root, timestamp, nonce and difficulty, and print its hash after mining three linked blocks
Simulate two miners finding blocks at nearly the same time, observe the fork, and count confirmations until one branch is orphaned
Simulate gossip propagation across a 30-node peer network with latency and measure how network delay changes the orphan rate of blocks

schedule.title: A minimal chain under attack
schedule.exercise: Reading-and-explain: list three guarantees a shared database with audit logs already gives and two extra guarantees a chain adds, with a clear verdict.

tasks.title: Write a minimal blockchain in Python or JavaScript with add-block and validate-chain functions, then validate a chain of five blocks
Attack your minimal chain by editing an old block, then re-mine every later block and measure the work needed against the number of blocks rewritten
Work through a case on a district records office and decide with evidence whether a ledger or an audited database better serves it, scored against a rubric

schedule.title: Consensus: proof of work and proof of stake
schedule.exercise: Short essay: compare the cost of attacking a proof-of-work chain with the cost of attacking a proof-of-stake chain, using numbers from the simulations.

tasks.title: Run a double-spend scenario on a small network and identify at which confirmation depth the merchant payment becomes safe against the attacker
Simulate mining with miners holding 10, 20 and 30 percent hash power and compare the share of blocks each wins over 1000 rounds
Configure a proof-of-stake validator set, inject a double-signing validator, and show how slashing and finality stop a long-range rewrite

schedule.title: Permissioned consensus and trade-offs
schedule.exercise: Fill in a comparison table of four ledger designs against security, decentralisation, throughput and energy, and justify each cell in one sentence.

tasks.title: Step through a Raft leader election with five nodes, crash the leader, and record which node wins the next term and why
Run PBFT with four replicas and one faulty replica sending conflicting messages, and verify that the honest replicas still agree on one value
Vary node count and faulty fraction in a consensus simulation, plot throughput against fault tolerance, and argue where the scalability trilemma bites

schedule.title: Wallets, keys and transactions
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page guide for a first-time mobile user on seed phrase backup, covering theft, loss and a family member who needs inheritance access.

tasks.title: Derive a key pair and an address from a random seed, and explain which steps are reversible and which are one-way
Trace a UTXO transaction with two inputs and two outputs, compute the fee, and verify that inputs equal outputs plus fee
Construct, sign and verify a 2-of-3 multisignature transaction with a time lock, then show that a single signature or an early spend is rejected

schedule.title: Smart contracts on Ethereum
schedule.exercise: Explain in prose how gas stops infinite loops, and estimate by hand the gas cost of a simple storage write versus a read.

tasks.title: Write a Solidity-style counter contract in the browser runner with increment and read functions, and record the gas used by each call
Write an escrow contract for a cocoa purchase with deposit, release and refund functions, then test each path with at least six test cases
Extend the escrow contract with a deadline and a dispute arbiter, then write tests covering the full state machine and its edge cases

schedule.title: Tokens, oracles and vulnerabilities
schedule.exercise: Audit exercise: read a short vulnerable contract on paper, mark every flaw, and write the fix and the attack for the most severe one.

tasks.title: Implement a minimal ERC-20 token with transfer and balance functions, and check that total supply is conserved across 20 random transfers
Reproduce a reentrancy attack on a vulnerable bank contract and show the attacker draining funds before the balance is updated
Fix the vulnerable bank contract with the checks-effects-interactions pattern and a reentrancy guard, then show a fuzz test finding no drain in 500 runs

schedule.title: Layer 2 and cross-chain bridges
schedule.exercise: Write a short explanation of why a payment channel needs a dispute window, and of why bridges have been the target of the largest thefts.

tasks.title: Open a payment channel between two parties, exchange ten off-chain updates, and close it on-chain with the final signed balance
Simulate a cheating party posting an old channel state and show how the honest party challenge within the dispute window recovers the funds
Compare fees and confirmation delays of 1000 transfers on a base layer versus a rollup batch model, and state where batching stops helping

schedule.title: Land, supply chains and payments
schedule.exercise: Case memo: for a rural land title scheme, list what a ledger fixes, what it cannot fix, and which legal and data-entry steps still need people.

tasks.title: Review a land registry case with conflicting claims and evidence, choose which records to trust, and note what a ledger would not have prevented
Trace a cocoa shipment provenance record, find where the oracle problem lets false data in, and select controls that reduce the risk
Model a cedi remittance through bank, mobile money and stablecoin routes with fees and delays, and rank them for a 500-cedi transfer

schedule.title: Do you need a blockchain?
schedule.exercise: Apply a written decision framework to three proposals (voting, certificates, medicine tracking) and deliver a one-paragraph verdict for each.

tasks.title: Answer the decision-framework questions for a university credential verification proposal and record whether a blockchain is justified
Evaluate a voting proposal against trust, privacy and auditability criteria, and write a decision with the evidence you used
Configure a permissioned network of four organisations with endorsement rules, then simulate a transaction that fails endorsement and explain why

schedule.title: Limits, regulation and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone report: describe your decentralised application, the tests you ran, and a justified conclusion on whether a blockchain was the right choice.

tasks.title: Review a fake investment scheme case, flag five fraud indicators from the evidence, and decide what to advise the victim to do
Compare Bank of Ghana, SEC and FATF positions on a crypto exchange case and recommend compliance steps scored against a rubric
Build a small decentralised application with a contract, tests and a front end, and measure throughput and cost against a plain database
